main_text.head: CONCIO PRIMA.
HAC DOCETUR ANNONAE CARITATEM & famem, divinitus imitti. Item quam dira & horribilis sit pœna fames.

p.i: Ex Oratione Salomonis quæ habetur 2. Paralip. 6. Cap.

main_text.p: 26. Quando clausum fuerit cœlum, & non fuerit pluvia, quod peccaverint tibi, & erraverint in loco isto, cõ-fesiq; [?] fuerint nomini tuo, & à peccato reversi fuerint, quando afflixeris eos.

27. Tu exaudies de cœlo, & parcas peccato servorum tuorum, & populi tui Israelis, cum docueris eos, viam bonam per quam ambulent, & dabis pluviam super terram tuã, quam dedisti populo tuo in hæreditatem.
28. Fames si fuerit in terra, aut pestis cum fuerit, aut ariditas, aut rubigo, lo-custa aut bruchus cum fuerit, aut cũ

page.notes: The faint mirrored text at the top ("DE ANNONAE CARITATE") is show-through from the reverse side and is left out. The word after "cõ-" in verse 26 is printed as "fesiq" with a mark that I cannot read with certainty; it is marked [?]. The hyphen in "lo-custa" at the line end of verse 28 is hard to see and may be absent in print. The page ends mid-sentence at "aut cũ", so the paragraph continues on the next page. No running head or catchword is printed.
